title: Capacity onboarding playbook - NA/EU/APAC (Q1 2028)
summary: Sprint-aligned playbook for staged GPU pool onboarding across NA, EU, and APAC with utilization targets, buffer windows, gating criteria, and cross-team action items. Focused on H100/A100/L4x mixes and prioritized by customer tier and latency zones.
content:
Purpose:
This sheet defines three phased rollout scenarios (Conservative, Target, Accelerated) for Q1 2028 to expand Redwood's inference capacity across North America, Europe, and APAC. It includes per-region GPU mix, target utilization bands, onboarding windows, operational gating checks, risks, and finance/SRE asks.

Executive summary:
- Objective: Add capacity to support a projected 35–60% increase in peak token throughput across hosted and dedicated tiers while maintaining p95 latency SLOs.
- Approach: Staged pool activations with regional traffic shaping, canary routes, and cross-region fallback.
- Key metrics: target steady-state utilization 65% (range 55–75%), minimum spare buffer 15% for burst handling, rollout cadence 2–4 weeks per tranche depending on scenario.

Phases and windows (high level):
- Phase 0 (prep): network tests, KMS access validation, AMI bake, infra-as-code templates locked (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (alpha): small pool activations in 2 AZs per region, internal load tests, verify KV cache behavior (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (beta): scale to 40–60% of path capacity, enable canary routing for 5% customer traffic (3 weeks)
- Phase 3 (general availability): full pool activation, autoscale policies live, cost monitoring and rolling alerts (ongoing)

Per-region capacity table (textual):
- North America:
  - Planned GPU mix: 60% H100 (4x48GB), 30% A100 (80GB), 10% L40s (for low-latency embeddings).
  - Target tranches: 100 H100 equiv -> 200 H100 equiv -> final 450 H100 equiv (illustrative).
  - Steady-state target utilization: 60–70%.
  - Peak buffer: 15% reserved for burst windows; procurement lead time baked in.
  - Rollout window: Feb 6 -> Mar 20 (Conservative), Jan 22 -> Mar 12 (Target), Jan 8 -> Feb 26 (Accelerated).

- Europe (EU):
  - Planned GPU mix: 50% H100, 40% A100, 10% L40s.
  - Tranches: smaller initial tranche due to networking constraints: 50 -> 150 -> 320 H100 equiv.
  - Steady-state utilization: 58–68%.
  - Peak buffer: 18% to mitigate cross-border capacity variability.
  - Rollout window: Feb 20 -> Apr 2 (Conservative), Feb 5 -> Mar 18 (Target), Jan 29 -> Mar 5 (Accelerated).

- APAC:
  - Planned GPU mix: 40% H100, 40% L40s (latency-optimized), 20% A100 for cost-sensitive workloads.
  - Tranches: 40 -> 120 -> 260 H100 equiv (regional vendor constraints).
  - Steady-state utilization: 62–72% (expect heavier tail traffic during local business hours).
  - Peak buffer: 20% (higher to account for vendor quota variability).
  - Rollout window: Mar 1 -> Apr 15 (Conservative), Feb 12 -> Mar 25 (Target), Jan 30 -> Mar 10 (Accelerated).

Scenario definitions and triggers:
- Conservative: slower cadence, higher verification gates. Trigger if procurement lead times exceed 6 weeks or if SRE headcount limited.
- Target: default plan — balanced risk. Triggered if vendor confirmations received and net-new enterprise demand projection is stable.
- Accelerated: compress windows, parallelize tranches, allow more aggressive canary percentages. Only if finance approves incremental spend and networking validation completes early.

Gating checklist (must pass before trunk activation):
1) AMI and driver stack validated against the model kernel set (pass/fail).
2) KV cache functional tests with synthetic sequences (p95 token times within 10% of baseline).
3) Network egress/private link bandwidth validated to support expected throughput at 80% utilization.
4) Monitoring hooks installed (per-route token-level metrics, GPU memory saturation, queue depth).
5) Autoscaler smoke test (scale up/down under synthetic traffic).
6) Cost guardrails enabled (budget alerts, per-route caps).
7) Security review: KMS keys available and audit logs flowing to central SIEM.

Operational runbook snippets:
- During Alpha: disable public-facing assignment for new pools; route internal traffic via canary tag.
- During Beta: enable 5–10% customer traffic, monitor output-quality regressions using eval harness.
- If GPU memory thrashing observed: immediately reduce batch size, apply model quantization profile B, and roll back canary.

Risks and mitigations:
- Vendor capacity shortfalls: maintain multi-vendor footprints per-region and pre-negotiated overcommit windows.
- Network saturation: stage incremental route weight shifts and leverage regional cache nodes.
- Cost overruns: enforce daily spend throttles and per-pool soft caps; finance to provision contingency budget.

Cross-team action items (owners and deadlines):
- Procurement (Aisha Patel): finalize APAC vendor LOI by 2028-01-18.
- Infra SRE (Jon Park): complete network egress tests and centerline by 2028-01-20.
- Applied ML (Emily Chen): validate kernel performance matrix for H100 + L40s by 2028-01-25.
- Security (Sana Iqbal): KMS access and audit pipeline validated by 2028-01-30.

Finance ask:
- Two incremental spend bands requested: $2.1M (Conservative) and $3.5M (Target) for Q1 capacity and buffer. Provide approval pathway for Accelerated (+$1.2M) if rollout is advanced.

Monitoring & success criteria:
- Primary: maintain p95 generation latency within 1.15x of baseline during rollout.
- Secondary: no more than 2% increase in error rates attributable to rollout.
- Financial: per-token cost delta vs baseline ≤ 12% after autoscale and batching optimizations.

Notes and decisions log (short):
- 2028-01-04: Agreed default to Target scenario unless vendor notices arrive indicating delays.
- 2028-01-09: SRE recommends raising APAC buffer to 20% due to provisioning uncertainty.

Open questions:
- Exact GPU SKU mix per cloud provider instance type (awaiting procurement SKU mapping).
- Whether to enable cross-region spill policies by default or keep them manual for first two tranches.

Appendix (quick reference):
- Contact list: Marco Rivera (owner), Aisha Patel (procurement), Jon Park (SRE), Emily Chen (applied ML), Sana Iqbal (security).
- Related docs: CONFLUENCE-4567 (capacity model), JIRA-INFRA-2319 (onboarding epic), procurement PR link above.
